# Metis onboarding in 30 minutes: option catalogue

Working document for the supplementary BRD on onboarding. Prepared 2 Oct 2026. Status: brainstorm input, not requirements. Market claims cite the research notes in `research/` (each claim there carries a URL, a date and a verification status); short source labels are resolved in section 7. An option marked **new** has no precedent in the sources reviewed, which does not prove none exists.

## 1. What is decided

| Topic | Decision (product owner, 2 Oct 2026) |
|---|---|
| Success measure | 30 minutes of hands-on effort by the main setup person until the "aha" moment: the workspace is active with the company's real lifecycle, real people are invited, the existing projects are in the registry and the executive cockpit shows real data. Deeper data (detailed WBS, capacity, process frameworks) follows, split among the right owners. |
| Inputs | Whatever the client has. Metis reads it, understands it, converts it to Metis data and imports it quickly; what is still missing is collected through automated Q&A or a better mechanism. |
| Users | Mostly C-level executives with little time. Any C-level must understand the process at once; nothing may discourage them into giving up early. |
| Who reads the inputs | Metis builds no model and trains none. It calls a third-party LLM through an API, enabled by the customer. That AI reads the inputs, talks to Metis's own MCP server to create the objects and records, and runs the Q&A for the gaps. |
| Guardrails | A user must not be able to steer the Q&A into revealing system, database, model or prompt information. |
| Second path | Prompts and guidance so the client's own LLM sends the needed data to Metis. |
| Fallback | Rule-based importers without AI (Excel, CSV, MS Project). |
| Output | A supplementary BRD plus supplementary wireframes, reviewed by GPT afterwards. |

Conflict to record in the addendum: BRD v4.3 lists "Hosting or training an LLM inside the platform" as out of scope for the MVP (`brd/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.3.md:390`). The decision above does not host or train a model, but it does make Metis send customer documents to an LLM provider, so the addendum needs a recorded decision, a sub-processor entry (BRD Section 17, data lifecycle) and a tenant-level consent.

## 2. Where the time goes today

| Layer | Who | What must exist | Steps today (GPT review round 2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tenant | Tenant admin | Sign-in (SSO or password with MFA), verified domains, users, roles per workspace and project, AI access policy | 12 to 24+ |
| Workspace | Workspace owner | Profile (11 fields), option lists, team and roles, lifecycle framework (stages, gates, approvers, quorum, mandatory artifacts, rules), process frameworks, portfolio tree | 18 to 35 |
| Project | Project manager | Project record, charter I to IV, business case, budget, WBS, assignments | 15 to 28 per project |
| Portfolio data | Resource manager, finance | Capacity per person and period, allocations, budgets, risks | not measured |

Source: `review/metis-review-vong-2.md:414-422`.

What the evidence adds:
- The four activation rules of WSP-14 are already met by a starter template once the team is invited (WSP-14 acceptance criterion 2). The time is spent on three things: a lifecycle that matches how the company really works, the right people with the right roles, and the data that sits in spreadsheets, decks and documents.
- Identity has an external clock: DNS domain verification can take up to 72 hours [atlassian-dns]. SSO needs the customer's IT. Neither belongs on the 30-minute path.
- Published PPM implementations take weeks to months: Celoxis 2 to 6 weeks [celoxis], Planisware 4 to 9 months for enterprise and 12 to 18 months for global rollouts [planisware], monday.com contrasts 6 to 12 months for traditional PPM with 2 to 4 weeks for itself [monday-ppm]. All are vendor claims. No PPM vendor reviewed claims a governed setup in under an hour [competitors section 18].
- Microsoft retired Project Online on 30 Sep 2026; after retirement customers can no longer access their projects in the service [ms-mc1478955]. PPM customers with exported plans need a new home now.

## 3. Design principles drawn from the evidence

| Principle | Why (evidence) |
|---|---|
| Show before you ask | The executive sees their own portfolio, built from their files, before answering anything. The AI setup builders reviewed all preview a draft before committing it [monday-magic], [jira-rovo], [planner-agent], [smartsheet-build]. |
| Never ask what can be read | Every value read from a document keeps its source; only uncertain or contradictory values become questions [flatfile-automap], [docusign-iris], [uipath-cartographer]. |
| Pre-select the best guess | Defaults shift choices (meta-analysis of 58 studies, d = 0.68) [defaults-meta]; in checkout flows, fewer fields matter more than fewer steps [baymard]. |
| Start part-done, keep it short, let them resume | A head start on progress raised completion from 19% to 34% in a field experiment [endowed-progress]; 72% of tours of 3 steps were completed versus 16% of tours of 7 steps (vendor data) [chameleon-2022]; unfinished tasks get resumed in 67% of cases [zeigarnik-meta]. |
| Ask the right person, not the executive | Nominate, approve and auto-approve at a deadline is used in HR software such as Culture Amp [cultureamp]; ask-the-owner requests carry context and an expiry [entra-consent]. If-then plans raise follow-through (d = .65) [implementation-intentions]. |
| Ask irreversible things first | ServiceNow warns that the fiscal calendar type cannot change after funds are allocated [servicenow-spm]. |
| Nothing is live until a person applies it | Plan, review, then apply is the market norm for AI-built configuration [stripe-mcp], [rippling-mcp], [servicenow-build], [pulumi-neo], and it matches BR-35 (prepare-only through MCP). |
| Everything can be undone for a while | Imports can be undone within a window [hubspot-undo], [linear-import]. |
| Business words for executives | The lifecycle designer stays for the PMO; executives see "how a project gets approved and by whom". Choice overload appears with complex choices and uncertain preferences [choice-overload-meta]. |
| Ask outside-in | Questions to an executive are about their own view, the decisions they keep and what they need to know; Metis derives the structure. How the company operates comes from documents or the PMO. Added after product owner feedback on 2 Oct 2026. |
| Numbers come from the client's data, never from the question | Thresholds and amounts differ per client; Metis computes a proposed boundary from the imported data and shows it as a consequence to confirm. Added after product owner feedback on 2 Oct 2026. |

Verdict legend: **Core** = in the recommended design; **Option** = worth a product-owner decision; **Later** = after Release 1; **Drop** = not recommended.

| Bring your own AI | The client's LLM reads its own files and sends drafts through Metis's MCP setup tools (the decided second path) | Smartsheet "Build with AI" from ChatGPT or Claude [smartsheet-build]; Wrike MCP lists workspace onboarding [wrike-mcp]; Asana preview tools [asana-mcp] | Core |

### 4.2 Reading and converting

| Option | What it does | Precedent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two-lane reader | Exact parsers for structured files (CSV, Excel tables, MS Project XML); the LLM only for unstructured content and ambiguous mapping | Layered column mapping with confidence thresholds [flatfile-automap] | Core |
| Source on every value | Each extracted value keeps file, page, sheet, cell and the quoted passage; every figure in the draft opens its source | Citations and confidence [docusign-iris]; source and verifier per fact [uipath-cartographer] | Core |
| Confidence bands | High confidence accepted and shown as "read from"; medium flagged; low asked | Auto-accept only above a confidence level [flatfile-automap] | Core |
| One project, many names | Entity resolution across files: the same project or person written differently in a tracker, a deck and an email | new for PPM | Core |
| Contradictions become questions | Two sources disagree (budget 1.2M in one, 1.4M in another): one question to the owner with both sources | Contradictions surfaced to an accountable owner [uipath-cartographer] | Core |
| Status and colour translation | Custom status words and red, amber, green cell colours mapped to Metis system states and health | Sections mapped to statuses on import [clickup-asana] | Core |
| Operating model from documents | Stages, approval points, approvers, thresholds and reporting cadence read from a PMO handbook, SteerCo decks or minutes | Gap: no reviewed product generates a governed lifecycle from documents [competitors section 18]; Planview suggests deliverables per phase and gate [planview-pa] | Core (differentiator) |
| Closest reference model | "Your process is closest to this reference lifecycle; these are the three differences", from a curated library (Company A, creative production and others) | Builders anchor to best practice [monday-magic]; UiPath ships 83 expert-attested processes [uipath-cartographer]; defaults effect [defaults-meta] | Core |
| Plans to WBS | MS Project and Excel plans become WBS items with dates and dependencies | MS Project import [celoxis-msp], [wrike-import] | Core |
| Kept-and-dropped report | Before anything is applied: what was mapped, what was ignored and why | Celoxis import list [celoxis-msp]; Meisterplan test import [meisterplan] | Core |
| Capacity and budget sheets | People by month in FTE, budgets and actuals from finance and HR spreadsheets | Gap: no reviewed importer handles capacity, allocations or budgets [competitors section 18] | Option (differentiator) |
| Charter from contract or SOW | Charter sections I to IV, key contacts, deliverables and client inputs drafted from a statement of work | Asana AI teammate drafts a brief from a deck and a transcript [asana-teammate] | Option (after launch, per project) |
| Suspicious content flag | Text inside a document that looks like instructions to an AI is reported, never executed | Prompt injection through stored content [supabase-trifecta], [github-mcp]; BRD MCP-16 | Core |

## 5. Three approaches

All three use the decided reading AI, the second path, the rule-based fallback and the guardrails. They differ in what the executive experiences first and how changes become real.

Note added 2 Oct 2026: the approved design (`2026-10-02-onboarding-design.md`, section 3.2) keeps the draft in the main BRD's Draft workspace instead of a separate "Setup Plan" layer; where this section says "Setup Plan", read "the draft held in the Draft workspace".

### 5.1 Draft first (recommended)

The executive drops what they have. Within minutes Metis shows the whole company as a draft rendered as the real product: cockpit, registry, approval flow, people. A "to confirm" rail beside it holds a short list of one-tap questions; a conversation panel takes free answers. One "Approve and launch" applies the Setup Plan: publishes the lifecycle, activates the workspace, sends the invitations and dispatches the remaining items to their owners.

Indicative 30-minute script (design target, not a measurement):

| Minute | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0 to 3 | Sign in with password and MFA; enable the onboarding AI; IT link sent for SSO |
| 3 to 8 | Drop files, paste, or record a voice note; a live feed shows what Metis is finding; the first irreversible questions (currency, fiscal year) appear while reading |
| 8 to 15 | The draft cockpit and the Portfolio X-ray appear |
| 15 to 25 | Up to ten question cards; any card can be sent to its owner; the approval flow is confirmed in business words with a dry run on three real projects |
| 25 to 30 | Summary of what will be created, what is assumed and who will be asked for the rest; "Approve and launch" (the aha moment: it is live) |

### 5.2 Conversation first

The onboarding is one conversation with the Metis onboarding AI, by text or voice, like an interview with a consultant. Files are dropped into the conversation; the product appears step by step in a side panel and each piece is confirmed in the conversation.

### 5.3 Delegate first

The executive spends five to ten minutes: drops what they have and names who owns what (finance, PMO, HR, IT, project managers). Metis runs a setup campaign: each owner gets a short, pre-filled task list with an auto-accept deadline. The executive watches progress; the cockpit goes live when the key owners have answered, usually after a day or more.

### 5.4 Comparison

| Criterion | Draft first | Conversation first | Delegate first |
|---|---|---|---|
| Executive time to the draft cockpit | About 15 minutes (target) | 20 to 30 minutes; depends on the conversation | Not in the first session; after owners answer |
| Feels like | Seeing my company in the product, then fixing by exception | Talking to a consultant | Assigning a project to my team |
| Reviewing 30 projects and 80 people | Fast: table and bulk confirm in context | Slow: long lists do not fit a conversation | Fast for the executive, slow overall |
| Risk of drop-off | Low: value appears before any effort | Medium: long conversations tire | High: momentum depends on others |
| Data accuracy | High: sources shown, owners asked for the uncertain items | Medium: answers come from one person's memory | Highest: owners answer for their own data |
| Fit with BR-35 and the publish check (GOV-21) | One Setup Plan, one approval in the app | Many small approvals inside a conversation | Many approvals by many people |
| Build effort | High: a draft layer across entities | Medium: conversation plus incremental writes | Medium: task routing and reminders |

Recommendation: **Draft first** as the backbone. It is the only shape that delivers value before asking for effort and that scales to a real portfolio. It absorbs the strong parts of the other two: the conversation panel from Conversation first, and the owner task campaign from Delegate first for everything after launch.

### 5.5 Product owner direction and refined flow (proposed 2 Oct 2026, awaiting confirmation)

Product owner direction: keep Draft first, and add from Conversation first the two or three questions that shape the client's main data structure before the drop; after the drop, Q&A for the missing data; then hand what is still missing to the responsible users, as in Delegate first.

Assessment: the direction improves the Draft-first recommendation. Some facts are choices, not data, and no document can give them (which part of the company to start with, how the executive wants the portfolio grouped). A structural misreading builds a wrong draft and costs trust in the first minutes, so asking first is cheaper than fixing later. It also serves clients with few documents. Three points of the direction, taken literally, would break the 30-minute goal; each has a fix:

| Risk if taken literally | Fix |
|---|---|
| The opening questions grow into a wizard | At most three framing questions; only facts no document can give, or facts that change how every document is read; business words; one tap; "let Metis work it out" on each; on the same screen as the drop zone; under one minute (design target). Currency, fiscal year, stage names, approvers and cadence are read from the documents and confirmed later, not asked up front. |
| Q&A waits until reading ends, so the executive sits idle | Questions stream in while reading, irreversible and launch-blocking items first; the executive cap (10 cards by default) holds. |
| Delegating items that launch needs makes launch wait for other people, which is the weakness of Delegate first | Launch never waits for a delegated answer. What launch needs is answered by the executive, assumed with a visible "assumed" badge, or set to a safe default; owners confirm or correct after launch; at the deadline the value the executive approved at launch stays (auto-accept never creates a new governance decision). |

Refined flow:

| Step | What the executive does | What Metis does | Design target |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frame | Answers up to three one-tap questions, or says one sentence instead | Sets the scope, the starting pack and the portfolio grouping; tells the executive which files help most | Under 1 minute |
| Drop | Drops files, pastes, forwards or records a voice note | Starts reading at once; a live feed shows what it finds | 2 to 5 minutes |
| Ask while reading | Answers the cards that appear: irreversible settings, contradictions, launch blockers | Applies ask, assume or defer per item; keeps the cap | Overlaps with reading |
| Draft | Sees their own cockpit, registry and approval flow as a draft, plus the Portfolio X-ray | Runs the dry run of the approval flow on three real projects | Around minute 15 |
| Approve and launch | Reviews what will be created, what is assumed and what goes to owners; approves once | Applies the draft: publishes the lifecycle, activates the workspace, sends invitations | By minute 30 |
| Delegate the rest | Nothing, or reassigns an owner | Sends pre-filled tasks with auto-accept deadlines; asks just in time later | Days, not executive time |

Confirmed by the product owner (2 Oct 2026): the refined flow and its three fixes; the sales-led pre-fill below is how the provider plans to run Release 1.

Framing questions, revised after product owner feedback. The first draft asked about the company from Metis's data model ("how do you group projects when you report to the board?"); an executive is the board's audience, not its reporter. Rule adopted: **ask outside-in**. Ask about the executive's own view, the decisions they keep and what they need to know; Metis derives the structure from the answers. How the company operates is read from the documents or asked of the PMO, never of the executive.

Facts pre-filled by the Metis team from the sales discovery (the provider operator records them when creating the tenant, TEN-01); the executive confirms them in one tap or corrects one:

| Pre-filled fact | Example | What it sets |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | All of Acme Holdings | Workspace boundary and how many workspaces |
| Main kind of work | Products and digital services | Starting pack (lifecycle family, process frameworks, option lists), MVP objects on or off (MVP-04) |
| Reporting currency and fiscal year | USD; January to December | Irreversible settings, confirmed first (evidence: [servicenow-spm]) |

The three questions the executive answers, each in their own voice, each answer showing a small preview of their home screen:

| Question | Answers offered (the executive's voice) | What Metis derives |
|---|---|---|
| How do you want to look at your portfolio? | By business unit or subsidiary; by product or service; by client; by strategic objective; by market or region; "Suggest one from my documents" | Portfolio and program levels (BRD 7.1), cockpit grouping, roadmap lanes |
| How involved do you want to be in project decisions? | "I approve every project before it starts, and any major change"; "I decide only the big or strategic projects; my team handles the rest"; "Our executive committee decides together; I am one member"; "I don't approve projects one by one; tell me when something needs me" | Approvers per approval point and whether a committee with quorum is used (GOV-03, GOV-05); for "big or strategic", a rule that routes those projects to the executive (GOV-06), whose boundary Metis proposes later from the client's own data and the executive confirms in the draft; the executive's place in My approvals (OVW-09) or only in the attention queue (EXE-02); routing of major changes, which uses CHG-10 (P1 in the main BRD; the addendum raises it to P0 unless the product owner decides otherwise) |
| What do you want to know first every morning? | Where the money goes and whether it matches our priorities; which projects may slip or overrun; whether we have the people for what we committed; what is waiting for my decision | Home view and cockpit order, which data Metis reads and asks for first (budget sheets, status reports, capacity sheets or approval lists), which freshness thresholds are set first (BRD 12.5) |

No preset numbers in questions (product owner feedback, 2 Oct 2026): amounts and percentages differ per client, so a question never carries one. When an answer needs a boundary, Metis computes it from the client's own data and shows it in the draft as a consequence the executive confirms or moves. Example for "only the big or strategic projects": "In your data, the 12 largest projects hold 80% of the budget; they start at 1.2M USD. These 12 plus the 3 linked to your strategic objectives will come to you. Adjust?" Without budget data, the boundary question goes to the owner of the budget data (finance or the PMO) as a delegated item, and launch proceeds with "strategic projects only" as the assumed rule.

One-sentence alternative, for example: "I want to see it by subsidiary, I only decide the big bets, and every morning I want to know what is about to slip."

Placed at "Approve and launch", not at framing: "Who will finish the rest for you?" (suggested from the documents, for example the head of the PMO). That person becomes the default owner of delegated items.

## 6. Guardrail stack for the onboarding AI (first cut)

Threats: prompt injection by the user (jailbreak, "show me your system prompt", "list your database tables", "which other customers use you"); injection hidden in uploaded documents; data exfiltration; privilege escalation; cross-tenant access; denial of wallet (very large inputs to burn tokens); off-topic use as a free chatbot.

| Layer | Control |
|---|---|
| Architecture | The agent has no database, file system or network access of its own. Its only interface is Metis's MCP server, under the confirming user's identity and tenant (MCP-04), with a dedicated setup tool group that writes only to the Draft workspace. No generic query tool, no code execution. Superseded by design section 5, which states the boundary from the customer's side. |
| No outbound channel | The agent cannot fetch URLs, send email or call other services, which breaks the "private data plus untrusted instructions plus an exfiltration path" combination [supabase-trifecta]. Cloud folders are read by a separate rule-based connector, not by the LLM. |
| Nothing secret in the prompt | The system prompt holds no credentials, infrastructure details, schema dumps or other-tenant data; it is written on the assumption that it will leak. |
| Documents are data | Extracted text is passed as quoted data with its source and never followed as instructions (BRD MCP-16); tool parameters come only from schema-validated extraction; instruction-like text is flagged in the X-ray. |
| Topic lock and probing detection | The agent answers only onboarding topics; questions about its prompt, tools, model internals, infrastructure, database or other customers get one fixed answer that redirects to the task; repeated probing is throttled and reported to the tenant admin. |
| Output screening | Replies are screened before display for prompt fragments, internal identifiers, keys and token patterns, internal hostnames, database terms and other tenants' names. |
| Server-side authority | Every write goes through the same services and rules as the application (write contract PLT-06, permissions, publish check GOV-21, activation check WSP-14); publishing, activation and role grants need a person in the app (BR-35). |
| Quotas and cost caps | Per tenant and per user limits on files, pages and AI calls (TEN-10), with a clear message at the limit. |
| Audit | Every AI call, tool call and refusal is logged with redaction and visible to the tenant admin (MCP-11, PLT-11). |
| Red-team regression suite | A fixed set of jailbreak, injection and leakage attacks runs on every release and every model or prompt change; the release fails on any leak, like the tenant isolation suite (TEN-02). |
| Provider terms | A data processing agreement with the LLM provider: no training on customer data, retention limit, region where available; the provider appears on the published sub-processor list. |

Note: the published sub-processor list names the LLM provider, so "which provider" is public by law; what stays protected is the prompt, the tool internals, the infrastructure and every other tenant's data.
